title: Importance-weighted latency-quality probe for batching + cache config changes
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a reproducible evaluation probe that measures latency vs quality tradeoffs for proposed batching and KV-cache configuration changes, but weighted by real traffic slice importance. The goal is to produce a single, explainable LQ (latency-quality) impact signal per config change that can be used in PRs and canary decisions. This ticket covers design, instrumentation, offline evaluation harness, and a safe canary rollout checklist tied to the signal.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible offline harness that inputs a config delta (batch size, microbatching, KV cache TTL/merge) and outputs slice-level latency distributions and quality metrics
A weighting scheme that maps traffic slices to importance weights derived from production telemetry and product priorities
A composite LQ score algorithm and visualization showing per-slice contribution to overall delta
Automation that runs the probe on PRs touching config defaults and surfaces a pass/fail recommendation for canary rollout
Canary checklist and playbook that uses the LQ signal alongside SLOs to gate rollouts
tasks: Design weighting scheme and expose config in eval harness
Instrument replay pipeline to sample representative traffic slices (synthetic + anonymized real examples)
Implement offline probe: run inference on baseline and candidate configs, collect latency percentiles and quality metrics (EM, ROUGE-L, hallucination rate)
Compute slice-level deltas and aggregate using importance weights
Build a dashboard tile that visualizes LQ deltas and per-slice breakdown
Hook probe to CI: PR check that runs lightweight sampled probe; produce artifact and recommendation
Write canary playbook and rollforward/rollback criteria based on LQ and core SLO breaches
test_plan: 1) Offline replay: For each candidate config, run 10k requests across prioritized slices (chat UX, knowledge retrieval, short prompts) and record token-level latency and quality metrics. 2) Slice weighting: compute weights using last-90d production traffic by endpoint and customer tier; normalize to sum=1. 3) Composite: combine per-slice quality delta (signed) and latency delta with configurable cost-latency multiplier to produce a final LQ delta. 4) Canary: apply candidate config to 5% of a low-risk tenant pool for 24h with traffic shadowing, run real-time probe, and abort on request-level quality regression > 1.5% absolute for high-priority slices or LQ delta worse than threshold.
results_placeholder: Offline runs pending. Initial synthetic sample (2k requests) completed with candidate config 'microbatch=4, kvcache_ttl=60s' showing +12% p95 latency for long-dialog slice and -0.6% EM on retrieval intents. Need weighted aggregate and further runs.
notes: We purposely use importance weights so a small regression in a high-value slice (e.g., enterprise search) outweighs trivial gains in low-value public demo traffic.
Quality metrics must be tied to ground-truth where possible; for generative responses we include synthetic human-labeled acceptability and an automated hallucination detector as fallback.
Latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) are measured at the token emission level for streaming endpoints and at request-complete for batch endpoints.
The composite LQ score will be parameterized: ops can tune latency_penalty_multiplier per release to reflect current cost sensitivity. Default set conservatively for runtime-1.24.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Small sample sizes on rare slices produce noisy weights. Mitigation: Floor weights and require minimum sample counts; flag low-confidence aggregates.
Risk: Automated hallucination detector has false positives. Mitigation: Use human-in-the-loop validation for first 3 canaries and calibrate detector thresholds.
Risk: Probe runtime expensive. Mitigation: run full probe in nightly; keep lightweight quick-probe for PRs with reduced sampling and expected higher variance.
